title: When Will the Bright Moon Appear?
synopsis: Explore one of the great works of Chinese literature from the brush of master lyricist Su Shi (1037-1101), discovering what the waxing and waning of the moon tells us about life down here on earth.

fullText.simplified:
《水调歌头·明月几时有》

    “但愿人长久，千里共婵娟”。每到中秋节，许多中国人都会想起这句词。它出自宋代文学家苏轼的名作——《水调歌头・明月几时有》。
    《水调歌头・明月几时有》是苏轼在中秋节的时候写的。当时，他和他弟弟已经七年没有见面了。中秋节团圆之际，他看着圆圆的月亮，非常想念自己远方的弟弟，于是写下了这首词。
    这首词分上下两片。上片是：明月几时有？把酒问青天。不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年。我欲乘风归去，又恐琼楼玉宇，高处不胜寒。起舞弄清影，何似在人间。
    第一句的“明月几时有？把酒问青天”中，“几时”意思是什么时候，“把酒”意思是手握酒杯。这一句写出了作者状态：手握着酒杯问天空“明月是什么时候开始出现的？”
    接下来作者望着明月，想象自己飞进了月宫：“不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年。我欲乘风归去，又恐琼楼玉宇，高处不胜寒。”在中国传统文化中，人们认为月亮上有漂亮的宫殿和仙女。这句词的意思是：不知道天上的宫殿，此时是何年何月。我想乘着风飞到天上去，但又害怕那里美丽的宫殿太高了，自己受不了寒冷。
    最后，作者从幻想回到现实：“起舞弄清影，何似在人间。”他想象自己在月光下跳舞，看着自己的影子，他觉得：享受人间，这不是比在天上更好吗？
    上片描绘了苏轼对月亮的遐想，并表现了他对现实生活的珍惜。下片则由月光的移动写起，逐渐引出作者对人生聚散的思考。
    下片词是：转朱阁，低绮户，照无眠。不应有恨，何事长向别时圆？人有悲欢离合，月有阴晴圆缺，此事古难全。但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。
    “转朱阁，低绮户，照无眠”中，“朱阁”是红色的楼，“绮户”是雕花的窗户，“无眠”是失眠的人，意思是：月亮转过红楼和雕花窗，照在失眠的人脸上。
    “不应有恨，何事长向别时圆？”意思是：我不应该有恨意，但是为什么月亮总在离别的时候这么圆呢？
    这让作者想到人生的聚散无常，于是写下了这首词中最著名的句子：“人有悲欢离合，月有阴晴圆缺，此事古难全。但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。”“婵娟”在汉语中是月亮的雅称，这句话的意思是：人生中有高兴和伤心，有相聚和分别；月亮也有阴晴圆缺。这些事情，自古以来就没有完美的答案。我只希望亲人们长久健康，虽然相隔千里，但都能一起欣赏这美丽的月光。
    这首词表达了作者对亲人的思念，也思考了人生的聚散。作者用月亮来比喻人生，告诉我们世界上很多事情无法控制，但最重要的是珍惜现在。希望大家都能健康平安，即使相隔很远，也能在同一轮明月下思念彼此。
    这种对亲人的思念，是人类共同的情感，也让这首词至今仍充满生命力。现代作曲家根据这首词谱曲，由王菲演唱，歌名为《但愿人长久》，是一首家喻户晓的中秋经典。
fullText.traditional:
《水調歌頭·明月幾時有》

    “但願人長久，千里共嬋娟”。每到中秋節，許多中國人都會想起這句詞。它出自宋代文學家蘇軾的名作——《水調歌頭・明月幾時有》。
    《水調歌頭・明月幾時有》是蘇軾在中秋節的時候寫的。當時，他和他弟弟已經七年沒有見面了。中秋節團圓之際，他看著圓圓的月亮，非常想念自己遠方的弟弟，於是寫下了這首詞。
    這首詞分上下兩片。上片是：明月幾時有？把酒問青天。不知天上宮闕，今夕是何年。我欲乘風歸去，又恐瓊樓玉宇，高處不勝寒。起舞弄清影，何似在人間。
    第一句的“明月幾時有？把酒問青天”中，“幾時”意思是什麼時候，“把酒”意思是手握酒杯。這一句寫出了作者狀態：手握著酒杯問天空“明月是什麼時候開始出現的？”
    接下來作者望著明月，想像自己飛進了月宮：“不知天上宮闕，今夕是何年。我欲乘風歸去，又恐瓊樓玉宇，高處不勝寒。”在中國傳統文化中，人們認為月亮上有漂亮的宮殿和仙女。這句詞的意思是：不知道天上的宮殿，此時是何年何月。我想乘著風飛到天上去，但又害怕那裡美麗的宮殿太高了，自己受不了寒冷。
    最後，作者從幻想回到現實：“起舞弄清影，何似在人間。”他想像自己在月光下跳舞，看著自己的影子，他覺得：享受人間，這不是比在天上更好嗎？
    上片描繪了蘇軾對月亮的遐想，並表現了他對現實生活的珍惜。下片則由月光的移動寫起，逐漸引出作者對人生聚散的思考。
    下片詞是：轉朱閣，低綺戶，照無眠。不應有恨，何事長向別時圓？人有悲歡離合，月有陰晴圓缺，此事古難全。但願人長久，千里共嬋娟。
    “轉朱閣，低綺戶，照無眠”中，“朱閣”是紅色的樓，“綺戶”是雕花的窗戶，“無眠”是失眠的人，意思是：月亮轉過紅樓和雕花窗，照在失眠的人臉上。
    “不應有恨，何事長向別時圓？”意思是：我不應該有恨意，但是為什麼月亮總在離別的時候這麼圓呢？
    這讓作者想到人生的聚散無常，於是寫下了這首詞中最著名的句子：“人有悲歡離合，月有陰晴圓缺，此事古難全。但願人長久，千里共嬋娟。”“嬋娟”在漢語中是月亮的雅稱，這句話的意思是：人生中有高興和傷心，有相聚和分別；月亮也有陰晴圓缺。這些事情，自古以來就沒有完美的答案。我只希望親人們長久健康，雖然相隔千里，但都能一起欣賞這美麗的月光。
    這首詞表達了作者對親人的思念，也思考了人生的聚散。作者用月亮來比喻人生，告訴我們世界上很多事情無法控制，但最重要的是珍惜現在。希望大家都能健康平安，即使相隔很遠，也能在同一輪明月下思念彼此。
    這種對親人的思念，是人類共同的情感，也讓這首詞至今仍充滿生命力。現代作曲家根據這首詞譜曲，由王菲演唱，歌名為《但願人長久》，是一首家喻戶曉的中秋經典。

sentences.simplified: “朱阁”是红色的楼，“绮户”是雕花的窗户，“无眠”是失眠的人，
sentences.traditional: “朱閣”是紅色的樓，“綺戶”是雕花的窗戶，“無眠”是失眠的人，
sentences.pinyin: zhū gé shì hóng sè de lóu qǐ hù shì diāo huā de chuāng hu wú mián shì shī mián de rén
sentences.english: In the line “Rounding the red pavilion, lowering into the latticed window, shining on the sleepless”, ..

sentences.simplified: 意思是：月亮转过红楼和雕花窗，照在失眠的人脸上。
sentences.traditional: 意思是：月亮轉過紅樓和雕花窗，照在失眠的人臉上。
sentences.pinyin: yì si shì yuè liang zhuàn guò hóng lóu hé diāo huā chuāng zhào zài shī mián de rén liǎn shang
sentences.english: .. “朱阁” refers to a red pavilion, “绮户” refers to carved latticed windows, and “无眠” refers to those who cannot sleep.
The meaning is: the moon revolves around the red pavilion and the latticed windows, shining on the face of those who cannot sleep.

sentences.simplified: “不应有恨，何事长向别时圆？”意思是：
sentences.traditional: “不應有恨，何事長向別時圓？”意思是：
sentences.pinyin: bù yīng yǒu hèn hé shì cháng xiàng bié shí yuán yì si shì

sentences.simplified: 我不应该有恨意，但是为什么月亮总在离别的时候这么圆呢？
sentences.traditional: 我不應該有恨意，但是為什麼月亮總在離別的時候這麼圓呢？
sentences.pinyin: wǒ bù yīng gāi yǒu hèn yì dàn shì wèi shén me yuè liang zǒng zài lí bié de shí hou zhè me yuán ne
sentences.english: “Bearing no grudge, why does the moon always seem to be full when people are apart?” means:
I shouldn’t feel resentment, but why is the moon always so full at times of parting?

sentences.simplified: 这让作者想到人生的聚散无常，于是写下了这首词中最著名的句子：
sentences.traditional: 這讓作者想到人生的聚散無常，於是寫下了這首詞中最著名的句子：
sentences.pinyin: zhè ràng zuò zhě xiǎng dào rén shēng de jù sàn wú cháng yú shì xiě xià le zhè shǒu cí zhōng zuì zhù míng de jù zi

sentences.simplified: “人有悲欢离合，
sentences.traditional: “人有悲歡離合，
sentences.pinyin: rén yǒu bēi huān lí hé
sentences.english: This made the author think of the impermanence of life’s partings and reunions, and so he wrote the most famous lines of this poem:

sentences.simplified: 月有阴晴圆缺，
sentences.traditional: 月有陰晴圓缺，
sentences.pinyin: yuè yǒu yīn qíng yuán quē
sentences.english: “People have joys and sorrows, partings and reunions.

sentences.simplified: 此事古难全。
sentences.traditional: 此事古難全。
sentences.pinyin: cǐ shì gǔ nán quán
sentences.english: The moon is sometimes dim and sometimes bright, sometimes waxing and sometimes waning.

sentences.simplified: 但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。”
sentences.traditional: 但願人長久，千里共嬋娟。”
sentences.pinyin: dàn yuàn rén cháng jiǔ qiān lǐ gòng chán juān
sentences.english: In this matter, perfection has been impossible to achieve since ancient times.

sentences.simplified: “婵娟”在汉语中是月亮的雅称，这句话的意思是：
sentences.traditional: “嬋娟”在漢語中是月亮的雅稱，這句話的意思是：
sentences.pinyin: chán juān zài hàn yǔ zhōng shì yuè liang de yǎ chēng zhè jù huà de yì si shì
sentences.english: May we live long, sharing the beauty of the moon from afar.”

sentences.simplified: 人生中有高兴和伤心，有相聚和分别；
sentences.traditional: 人生中有高興和傷心，有相聚和分別；
sentences.pinyin: rén shēng zhōng yǒu gāo xìng hé shāng xīn yǒu xiāng jù hé fēn bié
sentences.english: “婵娟” is an elegant term for the moon in Chinese. This sentence means:

sentences.simplified: 月亮也有阴晴圆缺。
sentences.traditional: 月亮也有陰晴圓缺。
sentences.pinyin: yuè liang yě yǒu yīn qíng yuán quē
sentences.english: In life, there are joys and sorrows, partings and reunions, ..

sentences.simplified: 这些事情，自古以来就没有完美的答案。
sentences.traditional: 這些事情，自古以來就沒有完美的答案。
sentences.pinyin: zhè xiē shì qing zì gǔ yǐ lái jiù méi yǒu wán měi de dá àn
sentences.english: .. just like the moon is sometimes dim and sometimes bright, sometimes waxing and sometimes waning.

sentences.simplified: 我只希望亲人们长久健康，
sentences.traditional: 我只希望親人們長久健康，
sentences.pinyin: wǒ zhǐ xī wàng qīn rén men cháng jiǔ jiàn kāng
sentences.english: These matters have never had a perfect answer since ancient times.

sentences.simplified: 虽然相隔千里，但都能一起欣赏这美丽的月光。
sentences.traditional: 雖然相隔千里，但都能一起欣賞這美麗的月光。
sentences.pinyin: suī rán xiāng gé qiān lǐ dàn dōu néng yì qǐ xīn shǎng zhè měi lì de yuè guāng
sentences.english: I only hope that my loved ones remain healthy for a long time.
Even though we are separated by a great distance, we can all enjoy this beautiful moonlight together.

sentences.simplified: 这首词表达了作者对亲人的思念，也思考了人生的聚散。
sentences.traditional: 這首詞表達了作者對親人的思念，也思考了人生的聚散。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shǒu cí biǎo dá le zuò zhě duì qīn rén de sī niàn yě sī kǎo le rén shēng de jù sàn

sentences.simplified: 作者用月亮来比喻人生，
sentences.traditional: 作者用月亮來比喻人生，
sentences.pinyin: zuò zhě yòng yuè liang lái bǐ yù rén shēng
sentences.english: This poem expresses the author’s longing for his loved ones and reflects on life’s partings and reunions.

sentences.simplified: 告诉我们世界上很多事情无法控制，但最重要的是珍惜现在。
sentences.traditional: 告訴我們世界上很多事情無法控制，但最重要的是珍惜現在。
sentences.pinyin: gào su wǒ men shì jiè shang hěn duō shì qing wú fǎ kòng zhì dàn zuì zhòng yào de shì zhēn xī xiàn zài
sentences.english: The author uses the moon as a metaphor for life.

sentences.simplified: 希望大家都能健康平安，即使相隔很远，也能在同一轮明月下思念彼此。
sentences.traditional: 希望大家都能健康平安，即使相隔很遠，也能在同一輪明月下思念彼此。
sentences.pinyin: xī wàng dà jiā dōu néng jiàn kāng píng ān jí shǐ xiāng gé hěn yuǎn yě néng zài tóng yī lún míng yuè xià sī niàn bǐ cǐ
sentences.english: He tells us that many things in the world are beyond our control, but the most important thing is to cherish the present.
He hopes that we can all be healthy and safe, and even if we are far apart, we can still think of each other under the same bright moon.

sentences.simplified: 这种对亲人的思念，是人类共同的情感，也让这首词至今仍充满生命力。
sentences.traditional: 這種對親人的思念，是人類共同的情感，也讓這首詞至今仍充滿生命力。
sentences.pinyin: zhè zhǒng duì qīn rén de sī niàn shì rén lèi gòng tóng de qíng gǎn yě ràng zhè shǒu cí zhì jīn réng chōng mǎn shēng mìng lì

sentences.simplified: 现代作曲家根据这首词谱曲，由王菲演唱，歌名为《但愿人长久》，
sentences.traditional: 現代作曲家根據這首詞譜曲，由王菲演唱，歌名為《但願人長久》，
sentences.pinyin: xiàn dài zuò qǔ jiā gēn jù zhè shǒu cí pǔ qǔ yóu wáng fēi yǎn chàng gē míng wéi dàn yuàn rén cháng jiǔ
sentences.english: This longing for loved ones is a universal human emotion, which is why this poem still remains full of vitality today.

sentences.simplified: 是一首家喻户晓的中秋经典。
sentences.traditional: 是一首家喻戶曉的中秋經典。
sentences.pinyin: shì yì shǒu jiā yù hù xiǎo de zhōng qiū jīng diǎn
sentences.english: A modern composer set this poem to music, performed by Faye Wong. The song is titled “Wishing We Last Forever”.

sentence_translations: “Prelude to Water Melody: When Will the Bright Moon Appear?”
“May we live long, sharing the beauty of the moon from afar.”
Every Mid-Autumn Festival, many Chinese people will think of this line.
It comes from the famous work “Prelude to Water Melody: When Will the Bright Moon Appear?” by the Song Dynasty writer Su Shi.
“Prelude to Water Melody: When Will the Bright Moon Appear?” was written by Su Shi on the Mid-Autumn Festival.
At that time, he and his younger brother had not seen each other for seven years.
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, when families customarily reunite, he gazed at the round moon, greatly missing his younger brother.
Consequently, he wrote this poem.
The poem is divided into two stanzas.
The first stanza is: When will the bright moon appear? With a cup of wine in my hand, I ask the clear sky.
I wonder what year it is tonight in the celestial palace.
I want to ride the wind to return, yet I fear the palace of the moon is so high that I will not be able to bear the cold.
Rising to dance with my clear shadow, how unlike the human world this is.
In the first line, “When will the bright moon appear? With a cup of wine in my hand, I ask the clear sky,” ..
.. “几时” means “when”, and “把酒” means “holding a cup of wine”.
This sentence describes the author’s state: holding a cup of wine and asking the sky, “When will the bright moon appear?”
The author then gazes at the bright moon, imagining himself flying into the moon palace:
“I wonder what year it is tonight in the celestial palace.
I want to ride the wind to return, yet I fear the palace of the moon is so high that I will not be able to bear the cold.”
In traditional Chinese culture, it is believed that there are beautiful palaces and fairies on the moon.
The meaning of this line is: I don’t know which year or month it is in the heavenly palace right now.
I want to ride the wind and fly up to the heavens, ..
.. but I’m afraid that the beautiful palace there is too high up and I won’t be able to withstand the cold.
Finally, the author returns from fantasy to reality: “Rising to dance with my clear shadow, how unlike the human world this is.”
He imagines himself dancing in the moonlight, looking at his own shadow, and thinks:
Isn’t enjoying life on earth better than being in the heavens?
The first stanza depicts Su Shi’s fantasy of the moon and expresses his appreciation for real life.
The second stanza begins with the movement of the moonlight.
Then, it gradually leads to the author’s reflections on life’s partings and reunions.
The second stanza is: Rounding the red pavilion, lowering into the latticed window, shining on the sleepless.
Bearing no grudge, why does the moon always seem to be full when people are apart?
People have joys and sorrows, partings and reunions. The moon is sometimes dim and sometimes bright, sometimes waxing and sometimes waning.
In this matter, perfection has been impossible to achieve since ancient times.
May we live long, sharing the beauty of the moon from afar.
In the line “Rounding the red pavilion, lowering into the latticed window, shining on the sleepless”, ..
.. “朱阁” refers to a red pavilion, “绮户” refers to carved latticed windows, and “无眠” refers to those who cannot sleep.
The meaning is: the moon revolves around the red pavilion and the latticed windows, shining on the face of those who cannot sleep.
“Bearing no grudge, why does the moon always seem to be full when people are apart?” means:
I shouldn’t feel resentment, but why is the moon always so full at times of parting?
This made the author think of the impermanence of life’s partings and reunions, and so he wrote the most famous lines of this poem:
“People have joys and sorrows, partings and reunions.
The moon is sometimes dim and sometimes bright, sometimes waxing and sometimes waning.
In this matter, perfection has been impossible to achieve since ancient times.
May we live long, sharing the beauty of the moon from afar.”
“婵娟” is an elegant term for the moon in Chinese. This sentence means:
In life, there are joys and sorrows, partings and reunions, ..
.. just like the moon is sometimes dim and sometimes bright, sometimes waxing and sometimes waning.
These matters have never had a perfect answer since ancient times.
I only hope that my loved ones remain healthy for a long time.
Even though we are separated by a great distance, we can all enjoy this beautiful moonlight together.
This poem expresses the author’s longing for his loved ones and reflects on life’s partings and reunions.
The author uses the moon as a metaphor for life.
He tells us that many things in the world are beyond our control, but the most important thing is to cherish the present.
He hopes that we can all be healthy and safe, and even if we are far apart, we can still think of each other under the same bright moon.
This longing for loved ones is a universal human emotion, which is why this poem still remains full of vitality today.
A modern composer set this poem to music, performed by Faye Wong. The song is titled “Wishing We Last Forever”.
It is a Mid-Autumn Festival classic that everyone knows.
